{{Recipe}}

'''White House Honey Ale''' is the much-anticipated recipe to White House beer.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220711171805/https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/blog/2012/09/01/ale-chief-white-house-beer-recipe|title= Ale to the Chief: White House Beer Recipe|last= Kass|first= Sam|date= 01-09-2012 |website= The White House|publisher= The White House|access-date= 30-07-2022|quote=}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==

* 1½ [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] Kent Goldings [[Cookbook:Hops|Hop]] Pellets
* 1½ oz Fuggles Hop pellets
* 2 cans (6.6 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) light [[Cookbook:Malt|malt]] extract
* 1 lb light dried malt extract
* 12 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] crushed amber crystal malt
* 8 oz Biscuit Malt
* 1 lb White House [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] gypsum
* 1 pkg Windsor dry ale [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] corn sugar (powdered [[Cookbook:Glucose|glucose]]) for priming

== Procedure ==

# Place each type of hop pellets in a separate hops steeping bag.
# In an 12 [[Cookbook:Quart|qt]] [[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|pot]], steep the hops bags in 1½ [[Cookbook:Gallon|gallons]] of sterile water at 155°F for ½ hour. Remove the bag.
# Add the light malt extract and the dried malt extract and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# For the first flavoring, add the Kent Goldings hop pellets and gypsum. Boil for 45 minutes.
# For the second flavoring, add the Fuggles hop pellets at the last minute of the boil.
# Stir in the honey and boil for 5 more minutes.
# Add 2 gallons chilled sterile water into the primary fermenter and add the hot wort into it. Top with more water to total 5 gallons. There is no need to strain.
# Add the yeast when wort temperature is between 70–80°F. Fill airlock halfway with water.
# [[Cookbook:Fermentation|Ferment]] at 68–72°F for about 7 days.
# Rack the mixture to a secondary fermenter after 5 days and ferment for 14 more days.
# To bottle, dissolve the corn sugar into 2 [[Cookbook:Pint|pints]] of boiling water for 15 minutes. 
# Pour the sugar mixture into an empty bottling bucket. Siphon the beer from the fermenter over it. Distribute priming sugar evenly. 
# Siphon everything into bottles and cap. Let sit for 2–3 weeks at 75°F.
